issues.legal_issue: A tenant who sublets the premises to a partnership may remain in possession, and therefore continue to fall within the extended definition of tenant, if the tenant retains effective control over the partnership’s affairs.
material_facts: The tenant had leased the land and later sublet the entire premises to a partnership of which he was a partner.
It was asserted that the tenant was the partnership’s managing partner and retained effective control, but the record contained no categorical finding on that issue.
The premises had been used for a timber shop, and the tenant had erected superstructures on the land.
issues.conclusion: If the tenant retained effective control over the partnership’s affairs, he could be regarded as having retained possession of the premises after termination of the tenancy and could fall within the extended definition of tenant. The Court did not finally decide whether he had retained that control.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(4)(ii)(a) of the Tamil Nadu City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921, the extended definition includes a person described in Section 2(4)(i) who continues in possession after determination of the tenancy. The Court stated that effective control over the partnership to which the premises were sublet could support a finding that the original tenant retained possession. Sections 3 and 9 concern compensation for qualifying tenants and an application to purchase land, respectively. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.tenant_protection_ejectment_case: A landlord has brought an ejectment proceeding in which the occupant claims protection as a tenant.
predicates.premises_sublet_to_partnership: The tenant has sublet the premises to a partnership in which the tenant is a partner.
predicates.tenant_retains_effective_control: The tenant retains effective control over the affairs of the partnership occupying the premises.

issues.definition: When an ejectment proceeding concerns a tenant who sublet the premises to a partnership, the tenant’s continued effective control over that partnership may mean that the tenant’s status continues.

issues.legal_issue: When the record does not establish whether a tenant retained effective control over a partnership occupying sublet premises, the court may remand the matter for a finding on that fact before resolving the tenant’s statutory status.
material_facts: The tenant’s claimed role as managing partner and his alleged control over the partnership were material to whether he retained possession of the premises.
The judgment below contained no categorical finding on effective control, and the relevant evidence did not appear to be included in the record sent to the Supreme Court.
The partnership deed was said to be on the record, and the Court considered that the existing evidence, or further evidence if necessary, should be assessed.
issues.conclusion: The Court remanded the matter to the High Court to determine whether the tenant retained effective control, directing it to consider the partnership deed and other evidence on record and permitting it, if appropriate, to obtain or direct the taking of further evidence. Eviction proceedings were stayed pending further orders.
issues.legal_principle: Where a material factual issue has no categorical finding and the record is inadequate to determine it, the Court may remit the matter for a finding based on the available evidence and, if appropriate, further evidence. The Court relied on the possible relevance of effective control to possession under Section 2(4)(ii)(a) of the Tamil Nadu City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal_pending: An appeal concerning the tenant’s statutory status is pending before the Supreme Court.
predicates.tenant_status_depends_on_control_finding: Whether the tenant retained effective control over the partnership occupying the premises could affect the determination of the tenant’s statutory status.
predicates.record_lacks_adequate_control_finding: The record contains no adequate finding or evidence from which the tenant’s effective control can be determined.

issues.definition: If an appeal is pending, the tenant’s status depends on a finding about control, and the record does not adequately establish that control, the matter is remanded for that finding.
